evidence: The formation of a Ta oxyfluoride interfacial compound was observed and attributed to the reaction of TaF5 with SiO2, based upon previous surface chemistry studies. The XPS data in Figs. 1 and 2 reveal that both Ta and Si are in their metallic (zero-valent) states for the thicker films. The depth profile results reveal that F adsorbed on the growing metallic surface and was incorporated, if at all, to a negligible extent in the bulk of the film. The Si 2p BE of 98.7 eV ( Fig. 2) is lower than the BE of elemental Si 2p at 99.2 eV , consistent with the Si BE of the titanium analog, TiSi x, that has been reported at 98.8 eV. For the tantalum case, a shift from elemental Si of less than 0.5 eV has been reported; unfortunately, accurate peak locations are not reported and cannot be discerned from the published spectra. Nevertheless, it is reasonable to assign the 98.7 eV Si peak ( Fig. 2) to a silicide based on the titanium data and the fact that Si has a higher electronegativity than Ta.
